newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial stocks rallied to end Monday's session slightly firmer in futures-related trade and on the back of some late afternoon overseas buying.
Gold shares continued positive on a perkier bullion price and brokers said they expected the market to remain firm on Tuesday.
"The market turned around. Industrials were weak but there was some buying coming into the market and also some futures-related trade. That's what pushed the market up a bit," one broker said.

"Guys cannot watch the Dow Jones tonight because of the market holiday in the U.S., but tomorrow we expect the market will still be firm on the gold price. Industrials might also be firmer but the main thing is the gold," he said.
Gold was fixed at $343.60 an ounce in quiet European trading on Monday, up from Friday's afternoon fixing of $342.40.
The all-share index rose 21.8 points to 7,042.5, industrials ended 10.2 points higher at 8,315.5 and golds gained 23.6 points to 1,418.7.
Brokers said turnover on the day was reasonable at 600 million shares versus 620 million last Friday.
"We saw some big trades in De Beers," one broker said.
De Beers leapt 200 cents to 148.50 rand, Anglo ended 50 cents up at 277.50 rand after giving up some earlier gains.
Brokers said sentiment remained upbeat with the rand remaining strong.
"We have has some good rumours for the past two to three weeks and players are trying to sustain the market at positive levels," one broker said.
Another one said market players would also look to U.S. CPI and GDP data expected this week for possible direction.

"What the market will also be looking for is probably something to come out of the Societe-General conference (Reserve Bank governor Chris) Stals and other speakers will be addressing tomorrow," he said.
In industrial futures, the March all-share contract was last at 6,480/84 from 6,485, gold contracts were at 1,001/05 from 994 and industrial contracts were at 8,096/8100 from 8,075.
